domain_hypothesis.reasoning: The columns including InvoiceNo, StockCode, Quantity, UnitPrice, CustomerID, and Country are classic indicators of an online retail transaction dataset tracking sales history.

kpi_specs.name: Total Revenue
kpi_specs.description: Calculates the overall revenue generated from transaction quantities and unit prices.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT SUM(Quantity * UnitPrice) AS total_revenue FROM data
kpi_specs.reasoning: A single total revenue card is the primary high-level health metric for any commercial retail business.

kpi_specs.name: Monthly Sales Trend
kpi_specs.description: Measures total sales over time grouped by month to spot seasonality and growth patterns.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', InvoiceDate) AS invoice_month, SUM(Quantity * UnitPrice) AS monthly_revenue FROM data GROUP BY invoice_month ORDER BY invoice_month ASC
kpi_specs.reasoning: A line chart shows how sales fluctuate month-over-month, highlighting seasonal peaks and macroeconomic trends.

kpi_specs.name: Top 10 Countries by Revenue
kpi_specs.description: Identifies the highest revenue-generating markets globally.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT Country, SUM(Quantity * UnitPrice) AS total_revenue FROM data GROUP BY Country ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 10
kpi_specs.reasoning: A horizontal bar chart is ideal for displaying a discrete comparison of sales volume across regional markets.

kpi_specs.name: Top 10 Selling Products
kpi_specs.description: Rankings of stock items by the total quantity sold.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT StockCode, Description, SUM(Quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM data WHERE Description IS NOT NULL GROUP BY StockCode, Description ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 10
kpi_specs.reasoning: A tabular format is best suited for lists of products with identifiers and descriptions, keeping details readable.

kpi_specs.name: Average Order Value
kpi_specs.description: Calculates the average revenue generated per unique invoice transaction.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT SUM(Quantity * UnitPrice) / COUNT(DISTINCT InvoiceNo) AS average_order_value FROM data WHERE Quantity > 0
kpi_specs.reasoning: Average order value (AOV) measures purchase sizes, which helps assess customer purchasing behavior and retail performance. Filtering out negative quantities prevents return transactions from distorting actual order size.
